title: db_domain has an ADD-COLUMN door: additive only, owner-gated, never a drop or a retype
intention: store.add_owned_column(table, owner, name, coltype, *, default=None) adds one nullable column (or one with a literal default) to an owned table. It returns True when added and False when a column of that name and base type already stands. The owner alone may call it (Law 6). It never drops a column, never retypes one, and takes a bare type name and nothing else.
why: The librarian row-id migration (T5, orchestrator 2026-11-14) must give 39 live leaf tables a `row bigint` column (Akien's answer to Q#104: node ids are master row numbers). The store has a door for a constraint (add_owned_constraint) and one for an index (add_owned_index) and none for a column, and the_constraint_door_is_the_only_alter probe reds any ALTER TABLE outside store.py, so without this door the migration would be a hand ALTER around the owner gate. Additive only because a migration that can drop or retype is a general ALTER, which is what the door exists to keep out.
traces_to: Law 6 (the owner alone gates writes to its table), Law 4 (the schema door, not a convention), RULE 1 (the librarian reaches the database only through db_domain).
how: D1: add_owned_column in store.py beside the constraint and index doors: owner-gated like them; the name a plain identifier; the type a bare type name (letters, digits, underscores, single spaces, an optional (n) or (n,m), an optional []) none of whose words is a keyword that makes it more than a type (primary, key, unique, references, check, default, generated, constraint, not, null, drop, alter, table, add, column, select, insert, delete, update) and which Postgres resolves (to_regtype); an existing column of the same base type is a no-op (False), of another base type is SchemaChangeRefused; ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN built with sql.Identifier and, for a default, sql.Literal. D2: a proof, three teeth. A NOT NULL, a key or a CHECK goes through the constraint door afterwards.

measured.saw: store.py has create_owned_table, add_owned_constraint, add_owned_index, write, update, delete, drop_table and no column door; db_domain's the_constraint_door_is_the_only_alter probe skips only store.py

after the build: the three teeth read green on Windows, red unfixed (the door is absent); a retype of a bigint column to text is refused naming 'bigint'; 'bigint; DROP TABLE t' is refused and the table stands
measured.how: the new proof, bare, CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID set

measured.saw: UNMEASURED: that the 39 live leaf tables take the column by one call each on a populated database, and the cost of ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN on the largest of them (Postgres adds a nullable column without rewriting; a DEFAULT on a recent Postgres is also metadata-only, on older ones a rewrite)

outcomes.claim: the owner adds a column: it returns True, every existing row survives unchanged and reads NULL in the new column (or the default when one is given), and adding it again returns False
a non-owner is refused with OwnershipError and the column is not added; a table db_domain never created is refused too

a retype is refused with SchemaChangeRefused and leaves type and rows as they were; a type string carrying a statement, a key, a default, NOT NULL or an unknown type is refused and the table stands; the column list never shrinks; no drop or retype door exists

outcomes.text: the proof, one tooth per clause, over scratch tables the store drops at exit.
